coverage_of_risk.rationale: No tests exist at all, so none of the app's riskiest logic — data joins, filtering, sorting, URL state — is covered by anything the team owns.

evidence: app/ — zero test files, testLoc 0 per static analysis; grep for *.test.* / *.spec.* returns nothing
behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: There are no tests, so the criterion is at its floor by the rubric.

evidence: app/components/MovesSection.tsx:64 — compareRows' missing-values-last-in-both-directions logic would regress silently
app/lib/api.ts:39 — idFromUrl-style URL parsing and cached() failure eviction would regress silently

regression_power.rationale: A refactor of lib/ or the components would pass any internal gate; only the external acceptance suite (which the app doesn't own) would catch breakage.

evidence: app/ — no test files, hence no noise to evaluate
signal_to_noise.rationale: Rubric assigns 3 when there are no tests: nothing is padding, but nothing earns its keep either.

findings.issue: No test infrastructure at all: no test script, no runner (vitest/playwright), no test files; every behavior is guarded only by the external acceptance suite.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest for lib/ and component logic plus a small Playwright component/E2E smoke test; wire an npm test script in app/package.json.

findings.issue: Filtering, pagination clamping, and URL-state sync (buildHref default omission, page reset on filter change) are untested; a refactor could silently double-reset page, emit ?page=1, or break deep links like /?type=fire&generation=generation-i.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the filter predicate and buildHref/syncUrl as pure functions (extract them), covering empty/default omission and clamped out-of-range pages.

findings.issue: Client-side sorting contract — ascending first, second click flips, missing values last in BOTH directions, aria-sort on the active header only — is untested and easy to break (e.g. negating the comparator also moves nulls).
findings.suggestion: Extract compareRows/sortedRows into a testable module and test each column type with nulls, strings and numbers in both directions.

findings.issue: Moves aggregation is the densest transform in the app (dedup key method|move|level, method order Level Up/Machine/Egg/Tutor then alphabetical, default level-then-name sort, ?game validation, fallback to highest-order game) and has no tests.
findings.suggestion: Extract the aggregation into a pure function taking pokemon.moves + move records and test method ordering, dedup, game fallback and invalid ?game values.

findings.issue: Pure helpers (humanize edge cases like mr-mime, latestEnglishFlavor whitespace/newline collapse, dexNumber padding, displayValue em dash) are untested.
findings.suggestion: These are one-line table-driven unit tests; add them first since every page depends on them.

findings.issue: The species↔generation↔type join (alternate-form exclusion, slot-ordered types, species missing from a generation) is untested; an overlay with one extra Pokémon is exactly the scenario the spec warns about.
findings.suggestion: Test the join with a fixture list including a new species and an ID > 10000 form to prove both inclusion and exclusion.

findings.issue: cached() promise cache (failed fetches evicted, successful nulls cached forever) and mapLimit (order preservation, concurrency cap) are untested concurrency/caching logic.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test mapLimit preserves result order and that cache.delete runs on rejection.

findings.issue: Hidden-ability flag merge across duplicate pokemon entries (OR of is_hidden) and alternate-form exclusion are untested.
findings.suggestion: Extract and test the found-map construction with duplicate and out-of-scope entries.

findings.issue: Not-found behavior for invalid pokemon/move/ability/type names and arbitrary URLs has no regression net beyond the acceptance suite; API failure (apiFetch returns null on !ok) silently renders Not found rather than an error.
findings.suggestion: Add route-level tests that an unknown name and a deep bogus path both render the h1 'Not found' with a link to /.

findings.issue: Type-page Pokémon dedup/sort and damage-relation uniqueness/label sorting are untested but lower-risk (simple set operations).
findings.suggestion: Fold into a small page-transform unit test alongside the ability page logic.

summary: The app ships with zero tests of its own and no test tooling, so all quality gates are external. The riskiest logic — home filtering/pagination/URL state, the Pokémon moves aggregation, and client-side column sorting — is exactly the kind of code that regresses silently under refactor. Adding vitest for the pure transforms in lib/ and extracted page/component logic would be cheap and high-leverage.
